```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(model.validation)
```

`model.form` checks the form definition. `model.validation` checks submitted data against it.

This walkthrough uses the survey supplied by `model.form` and this package's example validation rules.

## Load the validation plan

Load the form, register the business callback, and read the process that lists the rules to execute.

```{r}
model <- model.form::read_form_model("examples/survey-form.yaml", "model.form")
directory <- system.file("examples", package = "model.validation")
callbacks <- new.env(parent = baseenv())
sys.source(file.path(directory, "business.R"), callbacks)
plan <- read_validation_process(
  file.path(directory, "survey-validation.yaml"), model,
  checks = list(total_count = callbacks$total_count)
)
```

Structure checks run first. Content checks run only when structure passes.

For your own form, use `write_validation_rules()` to generate its structure and field rules.

Keep handwritten business rules separate; regeneration preserves them.

## Supply data and references

Provide named worksheet grids with physical row and column positions intact.

List matrices preserve mixed cell types, including header text above numeric values.

```{r}
metadata <- matrix(list(NULL), nrow = 5, ncol = 3)
metadata[2:4, 3] <- list("001", "2026-10-03", "alice@example.org")
observations <- matrix(list(NULL), nrow = 7, ncol = 11)
observations[5, ] <- as.list(c(
  "STATION", "COUNT", "LENGTH", "UNIT", "ACTIVE", "OBSERVED_AT",
  "LATITUDE", "LONGITUDE", "OBSERVATION_ID", "QUALITY", "OBSERVER"
))
observations[6, ] <- list(
  "001", 2, 12.5, "cm", TRUE, "2026-10-03T12:00:00Z",
  -20.5, 55.5, "OBS-001", 1L, "ALICE"
)
observations[7, ] <- list(
  "002", 3, NA_real_, NA_character_, FALSE, "2026-10-03T13:00:00Z",
  -21, 56, "OBS-002", 2L, "ALICE"
)
data <- list(Metadata = metadata, Observations = observations)
references <- list(
  observers = list(values = "ALICE"),
  stations = list(values = c("001", "002"))
)
```

Reference values are supplied explicitly. The engine does not fetch code lists or registries.

For Excel files, `read_validation_workbook()` reads grids while preserving cell types and positions.

## Validate and inspect findings

```{r}
result <- validate_data(plan, data, references, source = "submission.xlsx")
result$status
result$complete
result$valid
```

Before accepting a submission, require `result$complete` and `isTRUE(result$valid)`.

Now submit a negative count and inspect the resulting finding:

```{r}
data$Observations[6, 2] <- list(-1)
result <- validate_data(plan, data, references, source = "submission.xlsx")
result$findings[c("sheet", "field", "row", "column", "message")]
```

Findings identify the rule, severity, physical location, submitted value, and expected value.

Missing prerequisites make validation incomplete. Check `result$execution` when a rule cannot finish.

## Export a report

Prepare report data once, then write the CSV files and HTML page into one directory.

```{r}
output <- tempfile("survey-report-")
report <- validation_report_data(result, model)
write_validation_results(report, output)
write_validation_report(report, file.path(output, "report.html"))
```

`summary.csv` records status and counts. `findings.csv` records problems and their locations.

Both files include metadata used by the HTML report, such as stages, sheet order, and field labels.

Serve the directory over HTTP. The HTML loads its CSV files and local `report-assets`; keep them together.

Use `assets_directory` to share assets across reports. Optional `stylesheet` and `logo` paths customize presentation.

See `?validate_data`, `?write_validation_results`, and `?write_validation_report` for the full contracts.

```{r cleanup, include=FALSE}
unlink(output, recursive = TRUE)
```
